phases.name: Story First
phases.goal: Play the story start to finish — every chapter and named mission, plus the early one-time moments.

phases.name: Strangers & Partners
phases.goal: Finish the stranger strands and the partner trophies while partners are still at your side.

phases.name: Activities & Skills
phases.goal: Sample every activity once, then master the skill tests: range, races, drones, fishing.

phases.name: The Leonida Sweep
phases.goal: Cover the whole map: cards, vehicles, garages, meditation spots, challenges.

phases.name: Heat & Platinum
phases.goal: Crime-spree cleanup, the last counts, 100% completion — then the platinum pops itself.

trophies.name: Vice Got a Price!
trophies.keyfact: Nothing to do directly — it unlocks on its own once the other 54 trophies are all earned.
trophies.guide: This one asks for no effort of its own: it unlocks automatically the moment the other 54 trophies are all in your collection. The sensible route is the roadmap's order — story first, stranger strands and activities in the middle, the crime-spree cleanup last — because the 100% completion gold, A Long Road, is the genuine last obstacle standing ahead of it. Save by hand at every phase boundary, so a single missed flag never turns into a whole second playthrough.

trophies.name: Just Like Paradise
trophies.keyfact: Gone Fishing opens the game — the first trophy almost every player will earn.
trophies.guide: Nothing here can be missed, and there is no reason to wander off before the opening mission closes — just play Gone Fishing through to its end and this trophy pops on its own. It opens the game, which is why almost every player earns it first. If a replay ever fails to award it, run the mission again from the pause menu and finish it cleanly.

trophies.name: Paradise Lost
trophies.keyfact: Chapter 1 finished — a milestone on the story road, not a skill test.
trophies.guide: Work through every story mission in Chapter 1 until the chapter-end screen appears, and this trophy lands. Chapters follow one another in strict order, so this is a milestone rather than a challenge — keep the main missions moving and leave the long side detours for the later phases, where the roadmap gives them room. Every chapter trophy you bank is another span of the Phase 1 spine in place.

trophies.keyfact: The VCIA Takedown mission at the airport — its neighbour is Catch Me If You Can.
trophies.guide: The VCIA Takedown mission takes you to the airport, and finishing it is all this trophy wants. trophies.guide: Operation Savage Glory sounds like a heavy-combat set piece, and you should still turn up with your best weapons and armour — but the trophy itself only asks you to finish the mission. trophies.name: A Long Road
trophies.keyfact: Gold for 100% completion — the last obstacle before the platinum itself.
trophies.guide: This gold is the platinum's gatekeeper: it pops when you reach 100% completion, and nothing else stands between the two. What counts is the game's own checklist — the story, the stranger strands, the activities, the collectibles and every counted feat this guide tracks. Follow the roadmap phases in order, and let the in-game stats page settle any argument; if one category stops moving, filter the tracker to it and the open trophies will show you what is left.

trophies.name: Cunning Stunts
trophies.keyfact: Silver: 250 stunts across the playthrough — let the total grow, then mop up.
trophies.guide: Two hundred and fifty stunts is the target, and every kind counts toward the same total: jumps, near misses, drifts, air time. The counter never resets, so there is no rush — most of it will happen on its own through story missions and free roam. Whatever remains, clean up late in Phase 3 at jump spots you can repeat, and run races alongside it: Earn Cash, Not Kudos hands you stunts for free.

trophies.name: Master of None
trophies.description: Try each type of activity once.
trophies.keyfact: One try at each of the 9 activity types — a sampler, not a slog.
trophies.guide: Nine activity types, one try each — that is the whole ask. A race, a fishing trip, an arcade game, a round of bowling, a drone race, a shooting-range challenge, a meditation, a stunt run, and one more of your choosing. One attempt each is enough, which makes this a taster tour of Phase 3 rather than a grind; tick each type off in the tracker as you sample it.

trophies.name: The Shootist
trophies.description: Earn a gold medal in all Shooting Range challenges.
trophies.keyfact: Silver: gold medals across all 42 range challenges — every last one.
trophies.guide: Gold medals in every Shooting Range challenge — all 42 of them. This one is pure skill, so pace yourself: get to know each weapon's recoil and the rhythm of the targets, practise the handling in free roam, and work through the list a few challenges at a time rather than in one long session. Save your sharpest attempts for when you are fresh. The total of 42 comes from the PSN-tracked count in the list we cite.

trophies.keyfact: Twenty race wins, each on a different race — no repeats.
trophies.guide: Twenty race wins, and the key word is different — winning your favourite race twenty times earns you nothing here. Rotate through the race list, keep a note of the wins you have banked, and pick a fast, stable car you trust. Learn each route once, spread the wins across Phase 3, and enjoy the side effect: every race throws stunts at Cunning Stunts.

trophies.guide: Eight finished strands is the ask — started ones do not count. Five of them already carry their own finale trophies: Andy, Kenton, Billy, Randy and Tyrone. trophies.guide: Fifty challenges — side objectives, from stunt totals to activity milestones — and most of them complete themselves while you chase the other trophies. Check the challenges menu early and let the count build passively. If you stall short of 50, pick the easiest unfinished ones (short races, single arcade clears) and knock them out in a batch.

trophies.description: Lose a 4 star Wanted Level with your partner and escape the heat.
trophies.keyfact: A 4-star wanted level, lost with your partner beside you.
trophies.guide: Partners may not be around late in the story — our reading of the description, not yet verified in-game — so do this the first time a partner is free in the open world after a story beat. Save first, build a 4-star wanted level with your partner beside you, somewhere with open roads and cover, then break line of sight and stay hidden together until the stars clear.

trophies.name: Retail Therapy
trophies.description: Rob 3 shops back-to-back with your partner without losing your Wanted Level.
trophies.keyfact: Three shops in a row, with your partner — and the heat must never clear.
trophies.guide: The streak is everything: rob three shops back-to-back with your partner, and if the wanted level clears between robberies, the chain breaks. Scout three close-together shops first, plan the route, save, then run them in one chain and keep moving between each one. Do it in the same session as Hot Together, while a partner is available — partners may not be around late in the story, which is our inference from the description, not yet verified in-game.

trophies.name: Gunslinger
trophies.description: Take down 5 enemies in a single use of Combat Focus.
trophies.keyfact: Five takedowns inside one Combat Focus — set the scene, then trigger it.
trophies.guide: Five enemies, one Combat Focus: set it up deliberately. Find a group of five or more, get them clustered, then trigger Combat Focus and chain the takedowns while it lasts. A busy story firefight works, but a planned attempt in free roam — a gang hideout, a police response — gives you control over the numbers. Save before the attempt so a near-miss costs minutes, not a replay.

trophies.keyfact: Rhinos are tanks — get close to one at high heat.

Raise your wanted level high in free roam until the military response arrives, then get into a Rhino — or survive one's attention — and the trophy should follow. trophies.name: Sneakthief
trophies.description: Rob a jewelry store without being detected.
trophies.keyfact: A jewelry store robbed clean — no alarms, no witnesses, no detection.
trophies.guide: Undetected is the whole condition: no alarms, no spotted cameras, no witnesses raising the alarm. Scout the store first in free roam — entrances, camera lines, guard patrols. Save outside, go in quiet with a silenced approach, take the goods and leave before anyone reacts. A detected attempt fails the condition, so reload the save rather than finishing a blown run.
